subject: Genetics
title: Huntington's Disease
description: A fast breakdown of Huntington's Disease for builders.

hook.text: A repeating stutter in one gene—CAG CAG CAG—slowly destroys the brain. Huntington's is caused by repetition.

buildup.text: The HTT gene normally has 10–35 CAG repeats. Above 36, toxic protein builds up. More repeats, earlier onset.

discovery.text: Huntington's is dominant. A parent with it gives each child a 50% chance. A test reveals fate decades early.

twist.text: Repeat length grows across generations—called anticipation. Children can get sicker younger than their parents did.

climax.text: No cure exists. Knowing your status decades before symptoms is both a gift and a burden few can bear.

punchline.text: Too many repeats. The gene stutters. The brain suffers.

quiz.question: What causes Huntington's disease at the genetic level?
options: Excess CAG repeats in the HTT gene
